title: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

sense.text:
Revelation 3 is part two of the message to the seven churches, and it opens with a little history regarding the seven churches out of the book of Acts. If you have never read the book of Acts you are not going to understand the epistles of Paul, and you are not going to understand the opening chapters of Revelation either. This is the establishing of the seven churches of Asia Minor: Pergamos, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, Laodicea, Smyrna and Ephesus, the green area on the map. We are going to find out who established them.

“And after the uproar was ceased, Paul called unto him the disciples, and embraced them, and departed for to go into Macedonia. And when he had gone over those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into Greece, And there abode three months.” You see that: he and they abode three months. Captains, we have to get on this level. We might not be able to stay a year, two years, three, Lord's will in the future, but at least three months. We stayed one month in Sierra Leone, and the brothers and sisters that helped us do that are definitely going to get their blessing when the Lord returns, and he may be giving you blessings right now.

“And when the Jews laid wait for him, as he was about to sail into Syria, he purposed to return through Macedonia.”

“And there accompanied him into Asia” This is what we want: there accompanied him into Asia, that green area, Asia or Asia Minor. “Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.” Those names mentioned that went with Paul to Asia Minor are the names of the men that helped Paul set up Asia Minor. Sopater was one of the Bereans that believed (Acts 17:10-12). Aristarchus and Secundus were of the believers out of Thessalonica (Acts 17:1-4). Gaius and Timotheus were of Derbe, where Paul and Barnabas preached the gospel (Acts 14:20-21; Acts 16:1). Tychicus and Trophimus were of Asia, where all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks (Acts 19:10).

When you read the term Greeks, most Christians will say, see, it is for all nations. But the Bible shows who the Greeks were: 2 Maccabees 4 and 6 show wicked men like Jason who made a covenant with the Greeks to bring the Israelites to the Greekish fashion, and laws under which it was not lawful to keep sabbath days or to profess yourself at all to be a Jew, and whoso would not conform to the manners of the Gentiles was put to death. That is the history the Christians are unaware of. And the white scholars know who those Greeks were. The Encyclopedia of the Jewish Diaspora, Origins, Experiences and Culture, volume one, edited by Avrum Ehrlich, one of the books they use in the top theology schools, says that in spite of attempts to show that the Jews in the western diaspora knew Hebrew, it is common knowledge that basically they knew only Greek; the Jews of the West knew neither Hebrew nor Aramaic, and their religious lives, including the reading of the Torah and prayer, were conducted solely in Greek. The Torah was translated into Greek in the third century BCE. In certain rabbinic circles the translation into Greek was viewed as a necessity of the times: the sages recognized that there were entire diaspora communities that spoke only Greek, and that these would be lost to the Jewish people in the absence of an authentic translation. That is why a lot of communities of the Israelites only spoke Greek; they were forced into that. And rabbinic literature almost totally ignores the vast western diaspora that existed at the time, which is particularly noticeable compared with the relatively large number of places in this diaspora mentioned in chapter 2 of Acts, in the chapters describing the journeys of Paul, and in the Pauline epistles, which give a comprehensive picture of the geography of the western Jewish Greek-speaking diaspora in the first century. So the scholars know that Paul was not going to all nations; Paul was going to the Greek-speaking Jews. This is the history our people don't know. You sit in church and be a dummy, a donkey, the Donkey of the Day, not knowing what this history is talking about.

So the seven churches were all following the teachings of the twelve apostles. They were set up by Paul and those men, Sopater of Berea, Aristarchus and Secundus of Thessalonica, Gaius and Timothy of Derbe, Tychicus and Trophimus of Asia, and Barnabas also; those were the key figures that set up the seven churches of Asia Minor, all under the twelve apostles. Did some of them start going off? Yes, some of them started going the hell off, just like today: across the various IUIC camps you see which schools are weaker than others, which are more advanced in teaching and understanding, which have more zeal and which don't. Likewise here. This is why Christ said to John, send these letters unto the seven churches of Asia.

precepts.why:
Sopater of Berea was the first name, so here is Berea. “And the brethren immediately sent away Paul and Silas by night unto Berea: who coming thither went into the synagogue of the Jews.” Paul went into a synagogue of the Jews. “These were more noble than those in Thessalonica,” The Jews that were in Berea were more noble than the Jews in Thessalonica. How so? “in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.” They received what Paul was teaching with all readiness of mind, but they continued searching the scriptures daily whether such things were so.

“Therefore many of them believed;” Many of them, and guess who one of them was: Sopater, the name we just read from Berea, was one of them which believed. “also of honourable women which were Greeks, and of men, not a few.”

Now Aristarchus and Secundus of Thessalonica. “Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where was a synagogue of the Jews: And Paul, as his manner was, went in unto them, and three sabbath days reasoned with them out of the scriptures,” Three sabbath days Paul reasoned with them out of the scriptures. “Opening and alleging, that Christ must needs have suffered, and risen again from the dead; and that this Jesus, whom I preach unto you, is Christ. And some of them believed, and consorted with Paul and Silas; and of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and of the chief women not a few.”

So out of Thessalonica, notice these people that believed: two of the names we just read, Aristarchus and Secundus, helped Paul set up the seven churches of Asia Minor. What always catches the eye is that you had chief women in the church; that is Titus 2, those are the chief women. And it talks about the Greeks, which we deal with a little later on.

Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus: the semicolon shows that Gaius and Timotheus were of Derbe. “Howbeit, as the disciples stood round about him, he rose up, and came into the city: and the next day he departed with Barnabas to Derbe.” To Derbe. “And when they had preached the gospel to that city,” When they preached the gospel to that city, Derbe, “and had taught many, they returned again to Lystra, and to Iconium, and Antioch,” So you have believers that came out of Derbe, such as Gaius.

Timotheus was mentioned with Derbe. “Then came he to Derbe and Lystra:” Here we go, Derbe again. “and, behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timotheus, the son of a certain woman, which was a Jewess, and believed; but his father was a Greek:” So the mother followed the laws of Moses, and then she believed, accepted Christ; but his father was a Greek. That is always the stipulation, and the Greeks are dealt with in 2 Maccabees.

Of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus: you have people that came out of Asia that believed. “And this continued by the space of two years; so that all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.” Jews and Greeks. When you read the term Greeks, most Christians will say, see, it is for all nations. But 2 Maccabees 4 shows what the Bible says about the Greeks.

This explains the term Greeks, and yes, Maccabees is canon. “But after the death of Seleucus, when Antiochus, called Epiphanes, took the kingdom, Jason the brother of Onias laboured underhand to be high priest,” Jason was a wicked Israelite who laboured underhand to become high priest. That wasn't his office, but he laboured underhandedly to become high priest. “Promising unto the king by intercession three hundred and threescore talents of silver, and of another revenue eighty talents:” He was paying for this office, big money. “Beside this, he promised to assign an hundred and fifty more, if he might have licence to set him up a place for exercise, and for the training up of youth in the fashions of the heathen, and to write them of Jerusalem by the name of Antiochians.” He wanted the Israelite men that practised these trainings to be called Antiochians. “Which when the king had granted, and he had gotten into his hand the rule he forthwith brought his own nation to Greekish fashion.” He brought the Israelites to the Greekish fashion. This is why the Protestants didn't want us to understand this: you had wicked men who made a covenant with the Greeks to bring the Israelites to the Greekish fashion.

“Now such was the height of Greek fashions, and increase of heathenish manners, through the exceeding profaneness of Jason, that ungodly wretch, and no high priest;” Jason was a wicked Israelite. “That the priests had no courage to serve any more at the altar, but despising the temple,” They despised the temple of God, “and neglecting the sacrifices,” neglected the sacrifices, “hastened to be partakers of the unlawful allowance in the place of exercise, after the game of Discus called them forth;” This was the origin of the Olympics. “Not setting by the honours of their fathers,” Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses and so forth; they didn't set by them. “but liking the glory of the Grecians best of all.” The Israelites liked the glory of the Greeks best of all.

“By reason whereof sore calamity came upon them: for they had them to be their enemies and avengers, whose custom they followed so earnestly,” Notice the wording, so earnestly. We dressed Greek, we spoke Greek, we ate Greek, we started to worship the Greek gods. That is what the Israelites started to do. “and unto whom they desired to be like in all things.” Our forefathers desired to be like the Greeks in all things.

While Jason was striving underhanded to force Israel to become Greeks, laws were being set up by Antiochus the king. “Neither was it lawful for a man to keep sabbath days or ancient fasts, or to profess himself at all to be a Jew.” It was against Greek law to call ourselves a Jew. This is the history the Christians are unaware of. TD Jakes is unaware of this, Creflo is unaware of this, and if they do know it and don't teach it they are wicked as hell, because they have everybody thinking that when you go to Galatians 3:28, there is no difference between Jew or Greek, so everybody is in. No: it is telling you they made laws that we couldn't call ourselves Jews.

“And in the day of the king’s birth every month they were brought by bitter constraint to eat of the sacrifices;” They forced us to celebrate birthdays, the king's birth. That was never the Israelite custom; that was never God's law, to celebrate birthdays. When you read about birthdays in the Bible some calamity always happened: Herod's birthday, and John was beheaded; Pharaoh's birthday. It was always some death, so honouring your day was always against God's law. So now here you are today, mostly you women: it's my son's birthday, can we celebrate the birthday? No, because death always followed behind that. We were forced to do that filth, that evil. “and when the fast of Bacchus was kept, the Jews were compelled to go in procession to Bacchus, carrying ivy.” You see that word compelled? They forced us to celebrate the king's birthday. We are not supposed to be celebrating nobody's birthdays; get it through your heads.

“Moreover there went out a decree to the neighbour cities of the heathen, by the suggestion of Ptolemee, against the Jews, that they should observe the same fashions, and be partakers of their sacrifices:” Ptolemee the Greek said we must observe the same fashions as the Greeks and be partakers of their sacrifices: when they sacrifice to Bacchus we are supposed to sacrifice to Bacchus, to Zeus, to Mercury, and so forth. “And whoso would not conform themselves to the manners of the Gentiles should be put to death.” The Gentiles there is making reference to the Greeks. Christians need to understand this: there were laws in place forbidding us to call ourselves Jews, forbidding us to call ourselves Israelites, and if we did not conform to become Greeks we were put to death. “Then might a man have seen the present misery.” Many of our ancestors saw present misery.

This is what they do. “There is neither Jew nor Greek,” They say, see, everybody is in. Listen: there is neither Jew nor Greek, why? Because they are one race of people. The Greeks Paul went to were the Jews who were forbidden to call themselves Jews and were forced to eat Greek, speak Greek, dress Greek, worship Greek. Paul had to undo all that madness that our people were in. “there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.” So what is Paul talking about? Unity. He is unifying the nation of Israel once again at that time. It is the same mission that we are on today, the same mission.

sense.text:
“And unto the angel of the church in Sardis write;” Angel. Look at Bible Hub on Revelation 3:1, at the very bottom: angel, from aggelos, a messenger, especially an angel, by implication a pastor. You see that? A pastor. So the scholars know who the angels are: it ain't talking about Michael, Gabriel and Uriel. It is black people that don't know. Send a letter to Michael? You ain't sending them nothing. Send it to the pastors that were set up over the churches; that is what angel makes reference to.

“These things saith he that hath the seven Spirits of God,” That is Christ. “and the seven stars; I know thy works, that thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead.” Now that is a cold statement about the church of Sardis. IUIC camps, all the schools: what you leaders over the camps need to do is say, is this us, is this me here in this camp? Christ made a very similar statement about the Pharisees: outwardly you appear righteous unto men, but within you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity (Matthew 23:28). So Christ said to the church of Sardis that Paul and those other men set up: send a letter to the pastor over that church, you have a name that you are alive but you are dead. Jude says the same of certain men that crept in: clouds without water, trees without fruit, twice dead (Jude 1:12). You could appear like a rain cloud and be fully empty; today you have men who appear like they have the wisdom and understanding of God, but within there is no rain, no water, no truth.

“Be watchful, and strengthen the things which remain, that are ready to die: for I have not found thy works perfect before God.” Christ is really getting on this congregation here, Sardis. He just said they are dead, now he says be watchful. What do they have to watch out for? Watch and pray that ye enter not into temptation (Matthew 26:41): everybody, every man, every woman, once you self-examine you know what your weak zones are, and you pray to the Lord about that thing. Man, know thyself. People ask us, what do you see about me? We only see about you what you allow us to see, but believe me, everybody in here, there is a part only you and the Lord sees. Christ gave the example of the Israelites sown among thorns, where the cares of this world, the deceitfulness of riches and the lusts of other things choke the word (Mark 4:18-19). You could at one time be alive, but in time you can become dead. That is what Christ is making reference to in Revelation 3:1-2.

Strengthen the things which remain: the little bit you have, are you holding on to it? Strengthen the little bit you have retained in your spirit. Jude says building up yourselves on your most holy faith (Jude 1:20). Our job as teachers is to give you the tools necessary; it is your job to build yourself up. It is like going to the gym: I can't lift the weight for you. You have to read four chapters a day, ask questions, take notes, because if you don't, what we read in Mark 4 will creep in and choke the word.

That are ready to die: notice he said the little you have left is about to die, so you better strengthen the little bit you have. Some brothers and sisters, when you first come you are joyous, you love being around the brothers and sisters, you love coming to the school, going to camp, doing the work. But after a while you get disenchanted; it starts to become a burden. That is the first sign of death creeping in. You better pray to the Lord. Keep yourselves in the love of God, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ; you better pray for mercy daily. And of some have compassion, making a difference, and others save with fear (Jude 1:21-23): with some spirits we talk to you soft, others we have to curse you out because you are at the brink of death and we can't sit down and talk all night with you. Don't think, oh, you're not in the love of Jesus. That is the love of Jesus: we are trying to save your soul. Something is wrong with your spirit; you married a demon over there and she sucked the life out of you; get yourself right.

“Remember therefore how thou hast received and heard, and hold fast, and repent.” What is Christ telling the pastor of the church to let the congregation know? Remember how you first heard this word, remember how you had that zeal when you first heard. In other words, examine yourself. Go back to the beginning when you heard this word. The same thing Paul said to the Corinthians, examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith (2 Corinthians 13:5), Christ said to the pastor of the church of Sardis. Jeremiah says it too: let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord (Lamentations 3:39-40). Turn again, because you are at a point of backsliding; your life is unfolding before your eyes, things are just going wrong. Examine yourself.

“If therefore thou shalt not watch,” If you don't watch, meaning what? It is not talking so much about watching what is going on out there in the world. He is saying watch yourselves, because he just said you are about to die. What are you looking at Russia for? What are you looking at China for? Christ said your spirit is about to die; you better examine yourself. “I will come on thee as a thief, and thou shalt not know what hour I will come upon thee.”

This verse is heavy because Paul had already taught in 2 Thessalonians 2:1-3 that that day shall not come except there come a falling away first, all twelve tribes falling and going into captivity, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition, Esau, the white man. So they already understood that Christ wasn't coming at that time. So what was he talking about? The last days, after the twelve tribes of Israel fall, after the man of sin is being revealed. So the spirit of Sardis is alive today. That is what he is revealing there, and this is how these churches are here today in Israel.

“Thou hast a few names even in Sardis which have not defiled their garments;” Meaning you have a few members, a few believing brothers and sisters, which have not defiled their garments. Out of that whole congregation Christ said you have a few members there that have not defiled their garments; some of them were good in Sardis, but not the vast majority. Their garments represent salvation: he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness (Isaiah 61:10); Israel is the bride, as if we adorn ourselves with jewels. And Ezra speaks of those sealed in the feast of the Lord who have received glorious garments of the Lord (2 Esdras 2:38-39); those glorious garments are twofold, literal and spiritual. So wherever this church is today in Israel, there are a few members who have not been defiled, but the rest of you better examine yourselves.

“and they shall walk with me in white:” The fine linen, clean and white, is the righteousness of saints (Revelation 19:8). That is what that white represents, the righteousness of the saints. So we are not to have our garments defiled; that is our spiritual clothing. “for they are worthy.” You had a few brothers and sisters there that Christ said are worthy to walk with him in righteousness, but the rest of you. He doesn't mention names, so the whole church needs to do self-examination: is this me?

The danger with black and brown people is we never want to take the bad that goes for us. We always say, oh, I'm the good one. Really, sir? Did you ever think for a second to consider that you might not be right in the eyesight of God? This is something we are always afraid to do. Somebody teaches a class, hey brother, stop teaching them weak classes about women rule the world, and he goes, I wonder who he's talking about, it's not me. All the time I have been in Israel I see that spirit, because you are trying not to hurt people's feelings so you just put it out there. Rather than say is this me, let me examine myself, no, not black people: I wonder who he's talking about, and you know damn well that was you.

“He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment;” He that overcometh: they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony (Revelation 12:11). That is really how we are going to overcome, brothers and sisters. Does that mean we don't have to keep the laws any more? That ain't what that means; a Christian will read that and go, see, plead the blood of Jesus. No, we have to do what Christ said to do. And our testimony is God's testimony that he taught us, according to Psalms 132:11-12; it is not your diabolical testimony. That means garbage to God, because you give your testimony today and tomorrow you give us the finger. Your testimony, men and women, is garbage, every last one of us.

“and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.” That is what we all want: we don't want our name blotted out of the book of life, and we want the Lord to confess our name before the Father and before his angels. Whosoever shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven (Matthew 10:32). Confess who? That Christ the black Messiah is the God, the Lord, the king of the nation of Israel who died for our sins. These Christians ain't confessing that; they are talking about a white man with yellow hair and blue eyes who just loves everybody. You are insane. But whosoever shall deny me before men, that is you, brothers and sisters in the Christian church, denying the black Messiah Christ who died for the nation of Israel; him will I also deny before my Father (Matthew 10:33). Christ is explaining himself.

“He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches.” When it says if you have an ear, because we all have ears, it means if you have understanding. What the Spirit saith: now the Lord is that Spirit (2 Corinthians 3:17). So the Lord is that Spirit; this is the Lord speaking.

precepts.why: Thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead: Christ made reference to a statement very similar to that. “Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men,” Outwardly you appear righteous unto men. “but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.” You see what Christ said about the Pharisees: on the outside you look good, you fit exactly what the scriptures say, but on the inside you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity, iniquity meaning sin. So Christ said to the church of Sardis that Paul and those other men set up: send a letter to the pastor over that church, you have a name that you are alive, but you are dead.

“These are spots in your feasts of charity, when they feast with you, feeding themselves without fear: clouds they are without water,” You see that part, clouds they are without water? If you ever see a dark cloud you may say to yourself, it is going to rain, but Jude makes reference to certain men that crept in: they are clouds without water, because you can appear like you are a rain cloud but be fully empty. Likewise today you have men who appear like they have the wisdom and understanding of God, but within there is no rain, there is no water, there is no truth. Your feasts of charity are the Sabbath day and any other kind of gathering that God commanded us to do.

“carried about of winds;” Meaning any time a doctrine comes, that brother or sister goes with it. “trees whose fruit withereth, without fruit,” Without fruits of the spirit; that is what it is making reference to. “twice dead,” You know why it says twice dead? Because before you heard the gospel you were dead in the world. You repented of your sins, you came into the truth, then somewhere along the line you allowed something to happen or interfere with your walk with the Lord, and now you are dead all over again, trapped up in sin. So now you are twice dead. “plucked up by the roots;”

He just said that they are dead; now he says be watchful, and strengthen the things that remain. So what do they have to watch out for? “Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation:” Watch and pray that you enter not into temptation. You know what is evil for you. Everybody, every man, every woman, once you self-examine you know what your weak zones are, and you pray to the Lord; remember he said lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. Watch and pray that you fall not into whatever temptation you struggle with.

“the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.” Your spirit could be willing, but the flesh is weak. So this is what you have to watch for. There is an expression that says, man, know thyself: you have to know you. Many times people ask us, what do you see about me? We only see about you what you allow us to see, but believe me, with everybody up in here, everybody listening, there is a part only you and the Lord sees. Understand that thing.

Christ gave an example about that thing. “And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word, And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.” This was the third type of Israelite that Christ mentioned; when you read verse 15 down to 20 there are four categories, and verses 18 and 19 are the third group. This group of Israelites hear the word, and the cares of this world and the deceitfulness of riches, then it says the lusts of other things, because everybody's lust is not money. You might think, oh, it's money; it says the lusts of other things. Some people have a lust for power, some a lust for sex; there is a multitude of various types of lust. And it says entering in choke the word that you had already learned, and it becometh unfruitful.

So that is an example of how you could at one time be alive, but then in time you can become dead. That is what Christ was making reference to in Revelation 3:1-2. And if you don't build yourself up, the cares of the world, the deceitfulness of riches and the lusts of other things will creep in and choke the word.

Strengthen the things which remain: when it says strengthen the things which remain, the little bit you have, are you holding on to it? Christ is saying strengthen the little bit you have retained in your spirit. “But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost,” Look at that: but ye, beloved, building up yourselves. Our job as teachers is to give you the tools necessary for what you need; it is your job to build yourself up. It is like going to the gym. I can't lift the weight for you. You are 300 pounds of blubber and you want to lose weight; I can't exercise for you. You have to build up yourself. Likewise in the scriptures the Lord says build up yourselves on your most holy faith: that means you have to read four chapters a day, you have to ask questions, you have to take notes, you have to do that thing, because if you don't, what we read in Mark 4 about the cares of the world, the deceitfulness of riches and the lusts of other things will creep in and choke the word. Praying in the Holy Ghost: praying according to the law.

The key is verse 21: “Keep yourselves in the love of God,” Keep yourselves in the love of God. “looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ unto eternal life.” You have to pray for mercy. You are looking for the love of God? You better pray for mercy daily.

“And of some have compassion, making a difference:” Some brothers and sisters we can have compassion on; we talk to you soft: hey brother, hey sister, you all right? That works with some spirits. And others save with fear: others we have to curse you out, because you are at the brink of death and we can't sit down and talk all night with you. We see you are about to die in the spirit, so now we have to deal a little harsher with you. So don't think, oh, you're not in the love of Jesus. That is the love of Jesus: we are trying to save your soul, brother. Something is wrong with your spirit. You married a demon over there, she sucked the life out of you, and you see your life dwindling away. Get yourself right.

Remember therefore how thou hast received and heard. You know this one: he is telling you again, examine yourselves. Go back to the beginning, Christ is saying, go back to the beginning when you heard this word. “Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?” So the same thing Paul said to the Corinthians, Christ said to the pastor of the church of Sardis: remember how you have received and heard, and hold fast, and repent.

“Wherefore doth a living man complain, a man for the punishment of his sins?” That is a question Jeremiah is asking: wherefore doth a living man complain? What are you complaining for? A man for the punishment of his sins: you did wrong and you are complaining.

“Let us search and try our ways,” You see what he says here: this is the same thing Christ is saying when he says remember how you have heard and received. Let us search and try our ways. “and turn again to the Lord.” And turn again. Why? Because you are at a point of backsliding. You see your life unfolding before your eyes; things are just going wrong. Let us search and try our ways: that means examine yourself. That is what Christ was saying to the pastor of Sardis. Examine yourselves.

You know why this verse, I will come on thee as a thief, is heavy? Because Paul had already taught this. This shows how these churches are here today in Israel. “Now we beseech you, brethren, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by our gathering together unto him,” All Israel is only gathering unto Christ. All Israel is not gathering unto no dude in Harlem or Philly; that ain't happening. “That ye be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as from us, as that the day of Christ is at hand.” They thought the day of Christ was coming then; Paul said no, it is not coming now.

“Let no man deceive you by any means:” Don't let nobody trick you. Paul said Christ ain't coming at this time, meaning the time that he was writing. “for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first,” All twelve tribes have to fall and go into captivity. “and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition;” Esau, he is the man of sin that must be revealed, the son of perdition, the son of hell. Esau must be revealed; the white man must be revealed as what he is: he is Esau, he is the man of sin, he is the son of perdition.

What does this have to do with Revelation 3? Everything. Paul just said that day is not coming except there be a falling away first and a man of sin be revealed, and Christ says in Revelation 3:3, if therefore thou shalt not watch, I will come on thee as a thief. So they already understood that Christ wasn't coming at that time. So what was he talking about? The last days, after the twelve tribes of Israel fall, after the man of sin is being revealed. “These things saith the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God;” It says he is the beginning of the creation of God: that is Proverbs 8:22 on down. Write that down in your notebooks.

“I know thy works, that thou art neither cold nor hot: I would thou wert cold or hot.” To be hot means to be fervent in this truth: like when you first come into the truth, you want to read every day, you want to learn every day. That is hot, that is fervent. Cold means you don't give a damn: because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold (Matthew 24:12). The love of many, meaning the obedience to God's law, shall wax cold, meaning you don't give a damn any more, you don't care. An example of that is you don't care when you do evil to brothers and sisters, then you go on Facebook and want to do a live singing concert. You the devil the Bible speaks of, with your head covered when you know the scriptures say a man should not cover his head, sitting there looking like an Arab, meanwhile you're Edomite with your head covered looking like a wannabe Arab. So the love of many waxed cold: that is you guys; you know who you is.

“So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth.” Meaning I will kill you. When he says spue thee out of my mouth, meaning Christ will kill you. You are not cold and you are not hot; you are in the middle. Elijah said, how long halt ye between two opinions? if the Lord be God, follow him: but if Baal, then follow him; and the people answered him not a word (1 Kings 18:21). They were lukewarm; they didn't want to choose God, they didn't want to choose Baal; they said we're in the middle.

That spirit is lukewarm; leave him or her alone. Guess what: God is going to bring in new spirits with fervent heat. That is the word, fervent heat: passion, that zeal. That is what is going to happen.

“Because thou sayest, I am rich, and increased with goods, and have need of nothing;” Laodicea was a money capital church; this congregation was about money. You have to examine that: Austin, DC, certain congregations where money has been the focus, those two in particular. Austin because of what happened there; that didn't happen in DC. And he that lacketh diligence, virtue, knowledge, temperance, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness and charity is blind, and cannot see afar off, and hath forgotten that he was purged from his old sins (2 Peter 1:5-9): those brothers and sisters that ran out of here traitorously are blind, and went right back to their evil. “and naked:” When the Bible calls you naked it says you are naked to your shame (Exodus 32:25). Blessed is he that watcheth, and keepeth his garments, lest he walk naked, and they see his shame (Revelation 16:15): you better have your spiritual clothes on. When I see you singing songs using the words of God with your head covered, I see your shame; you are so reprobate you don't see it, you little Ali Baba and the forty thieves head wrap, you simple brothers.

“I counsel thee to buy of me gold tried in the fire,” What does it mean, buy of me gold tried in the fire? The law of thy mouth is better unto me than thousands of gold and silver (Psalms 119:72): the law of thy mouth is the Bible, the scriptures. This is the gold that has been tried in the fire, because he said my word shall never fail. And buy of me: ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money; come ye, buy, and eat (Isaiah 55:1). Buy and eat what? The Bible, the word of God, wine and milk without money. This truth is not something you can buy; you have to pray to the Lord and he will give it to you, like it says in James 1, he gives wisdom liberally and upbraideth not. “that thou mayest be rich;” Not that carnal money you have, not the Bitcoin, not the dollars and cents, not the credit cards. He wants you to be rich in understanding his word.

“and white raiment, that thou mayest be clothed, and that the shame of thy nakedness do not appear; and anoint thine eyes with eyesalve,” What does eyesalve do? Like Visine gets the red out: Christ wants us to see clearly what the word of God is saying. Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law (Psalms 119:18): when we send up our prayers we have to ask God to give us understanding, open our eyes to what the word of God is saying, because many of these scriptures have two and three meanings. It is not talking about your physical eyes: the natural man, the sinful man, receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness unto him, because they are spiritually discerned (1 Corinthians 2:14). The Bible can only be spiritually discerned; this is a spiritual thing we are in. “that thou mayest see.” So we want the Lord to anoint our spiritual eyes with eyesalve so that we can spiritually discern what is written in the Bible. That is our prayer; that is what we want.

“As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten:” A lot of times we hate to be chastened. My son, despise not thou the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when thou art rebuked of him (Hebrews 12:5): don't faint means don't give up, don't run, don't say I'm leaving, I'm going back, I'm going to put a head wrap on my head and sing, you idiot. For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. That has happened to all of us and it is going to intensify; he is trying us. Deacon Malachi said today he sees in the spirit that things could possibly get worse here in Babylon the great for us, but the Lord is going to look out for us. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons: whatever comes our way, brothers and sisters, we must endure. You are not going to come into this truth and not be chastened of the Lord, only if you are an agent; but if ye be without chastisement, then are ye bastards, and not sons. Did you hear that, Weasel? God chastens us for our profit, for a divine, spiritual reason, that we might be partakers of his holiness; he has to beat certain characteristics out of us, train us. No chastening for the present seems joyous, like this thing going on now, but grievous: some of you lost your jobs. Just hang on in there; if it's food, we got you. And for you Negroes that talk about how 501c3 is so evil because you are getting government handouts: then don't take the government stimulus package, you black-ass devils, that is a covenant with the government. Afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness: once you come through that fire you can look back at the chastening and say God was trying to teach me something; hindsight is 20/20. Lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees: right now in the country hands are hanging down, knees are quaking; lift up your hands to pray, strengthen those knees, make straight paths for your feet, walk straight in the laws of God, lest that which is lame be turned out of the way. The brothers and sisters that left this truth were lame and turned out of the way, because when they got some chastisement they said I'm leaving, you're the devil, I hate you. And we glory in tribulations also, knowing that tribulation worketh patience, and patience experience, and experience hope (Romans 5:3-5): there is a purpose behind the chastisement of the Lord.

“be zealous therefore, and repent.” When you are being chastised you might not feel zealous at the moment, but Christ commands, be zealous therefore, and repent. Why does he say repent? Because obviously he is chastising you for something you are doing that you must self-examine.

“Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.” What is that talking about? Repentance. Christ coming in and supping with you: when you are breaking bread, drinking wine, he is coming into your spirit, your mind, your heart, your soul, and supping with you; he is sharing the spiritual understanding with you. If a man love me, he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him (John 14:23). That means the Lord is in your heart, in your soul, in your spirit.

“To him that overcometh” Here we go again, to him that overcometh. What is he saying to that church? He knows everybody is not going to overcome; that is why he stipulates, to him that overcometh. “will I grant to sit with me in my throne,” That goes with Matthew 19:28, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel. That was for the twelve; Revelation 3:21 is going with the 144. “even as I also overcame, and am set down with my Father in his throne.” Even as I also overcame. That is some heavy stuff right there.

“He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches.” That concludes Revelation the third chapter. We all have to self-examine. Don't take it personal if your congregation was called out; there are some things we have to work on, and New York, you're cheating yourselves, don't think we forgot about you either. It's all love, but we do have to fix our situations and make them that much better.

As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten. A lot of times we hate to be chastened; we do. Paul says the same thing here. “And ye have forgotten the exhortation which speaketh unto you as unto children,” because we are children, “My son, despise not thou the chastening of the Lord,” Christ said, as many as I love I chasten, I rebuke. “nor faint when thou art rebuked of him:” You know what it means by don't faint? Don't give up, don't run, don't go, I'm leaving, I'm going back, I'm going to put a head wrap on my head and sing. You idiot.

“For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.” He scourges every son that he receives. So that is what has happened to all of us, and it is going to intensify; he is trying us. “If ye endure chastening,” Deacon Malachi said today he sees in the spirit that things could possibly get worse here in Babylon the great for us, but the Lord is going to look out for us. If you endure whatever comes our way, brothers and sisters, we must endure. “God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?” What son is he that the father does not chasten, does not punish?

“But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers,” You see that: which all are partakers of. You are not going to come into this truth and not be chastened of the Lord. You are not going to be called into this truth and not be chastened of the Lord; only if you're an agent, and he wasn't called, he was sent. “then are ye bastards,” Then are ye bastards. Did you hear that, Weasel? Then are ye bastards, “and not sons.” You are not sons of God.

“Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence:” If your own earthly father corrects you, and I ain't talking about those of you with crackhead fathers or fathers on methadone, we gave them reverence. “shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?” The Father of spirits, that is the Lord. “For they verily for a few days chastened us after their own pleasure;” Your own earthly father would chasten you for a few days after his own pleasure: you didn't wash the dishes, I'm going to beat you on the sides and you don't get no TV for a week. “but he for our profit,” God chastens us for our profit, meaning there is a divine reason, a spiritual reason, for God to chasten us. “that we might be partakers of his holiness.” He wants us to be partakers of his holiness, but in order to become partakers we must be chastened. He has to beat certain characteristics out of us, train us.

“Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous,” Like this thing going on now; it doesn't seem joyous at all. “but grievous:” Some of you lost your jobs; this is grievous. Lord Jesus, help me, I don't know what I'm going to do. Just hang on in there, just hold on. If it's food, we got you. If everybody loses their job there is nothing we could really do, we go bankrupt, we'd be in the damn street, but food and clothes, we got you. The government said they are going to give out stimulus packages, and we are going to roll with that. And for you Negroes that talk about how 501c3 is so evil, so wicked, because you are getting government handouts: then don't take the government stimulus package, you black-ass devils. Don't take the check at all. That is a covenant with the government. You are going to take that, but we're evil? Yeah, right. “nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.” What does that mean? Once you come through that fire you can look back at the chastening and say, God was trying to teach me something; now I understand what he was trying to show me. I didn't understand it at the moment, but I see it now. Hindsight is 20/20.

“Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees;” Right now we are going through this thing in the country: hands are hanging down, knees are quaking, we don't know what the Lord is going to do. Lift up the hands which hang down, meaning lift up your hands to pray; and your feeble knees, strengthen them knees. “And make straight paths for your feet,” Meaning walk straight in the laws of God, in the plans of God. “lest that which is lame be turned out of the way;” See them brothers and sisters that left this truth: they were lame, all lame, and were turned out of the way. Why? Because when they got some chastisement they said, I'm leaving, I'm gone, you're the devil, I hate you. Now you are lame and turned out of the way, because you couldn't endure the chastening of the Lord. “but let it rather be healed.”

Paul explained that yielding of the right fruit of righteousness. “And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also:” There he goes again: glory in tribulations. We have to learn that thing; I'm still learning it. When hell and high water come my way, oh Lord God, help me. We have to learn this thing. “knowing that tribulation worketh patience;” See that: tribulation works patience. That is what we were just reading in Hebrews 12. “And patience, experience;” Patience brings forth experience. “and experience, hope:” Experience brings forth hope. “And hope maketh not ashamed;” Hope makes us not ashamed. Why? “because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us.” So there is a purpose behind the chastisement of the Lord.

I will come in to him, and will sup with him. What is that talking about? Repentance. Christ coming in and supping with you: when you are breaking bread, drinking wine, he is coming into your spirit, your mind, your heart, your soul, and supping with you; he is sharing the spiritual understanding with you. “Jesus answered and said unto him, If a man love me, he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we will come unto him,” And we will come unto him, “and make our abode with him.” We will make our abode with him. That means what? In your heart. The Lord is in your heart, in your soul, in your spirit.

To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne; that goes with Matthew 19:28. “And Jesus said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.” You see that: so that was for the twelve. Revelation 3:21 is going with the 144: to him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame.

sense.text:
Brothers and sisters, remember a year or two ago, when that doctrine about morning-to-morning Sabbath came out: there are going to be a lot more, and eventually they are going to tell you not to keep the law. This week that is exactly what happened. The brother said Passover means nothing, it doesn't matter if you keep Passover or not; he said if you keep the atonement, that means the death of Christ means nothing. Didn't Paul keep it in the book of Acts? Yes. He claims we are going to learn again, Christ is going to teach us together in the wilderness. You are not going to make it in the wilderness, and here is the proof. Some of you actually believe that if you keep the atonement the death of Christ means nothing. Basically he is saying you don't have to keep the laws, you cannot keep the laws, Christ took everything from us, remove all the high holidays, you don't have to keep Passover, you don't have to keep none of those things. That is exactly what he is saying, and you were warned that was going to happen. You know what he tried to do? He tried to turn you back to Christianity. Next he is going to say the Catholic church is nothing, you can go to the Catholic church.

“Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” It says seal the law among my disciples. Revelation 7:3-4 shows the servants of our God sealed in their foreheads: you cannot be sealed if you are not keeping the law. You can only get sealed with the law. Go ahead and believe him if you want to, but one thing is sure: the Most High is going to bring heavy judgment on that brother. You are making Israel break the law. Wait for it; mark my words, you are going to have some heavy, heavy judgment come on you. Just watch, Israel, watch. He hasn't learned nothing yet. Christ made that comment about the little ones: you are making Israel break the law, and heavy judgment is coming upon you. Wait for it.

Seal the law among my disciples. “Saying, Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” You cannot be sealed if you are not keeping the law. You can only get sealed with the law; that is what he is talking about.

“And I heard the number of them which were sealed:” Sealed with what? With the law. “and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” This is talking about the leaders, and of course when you keep reading down he is going to say a multitude no man can number; that is talking about the children of Israel. We must be sealed with the law. So if you say don't keep the law, you might as well go back to Christianity, because that is what the pastor is teaching: don't keep the laws. If you are saying that if you keep the law the death of Christ means nothing, you might as well say go back to the Catholic church, go back to the Christian church. That is exactly what you are saying.
